name: Arab Conquest of Central Asia and Sind
summary: Umayyad general Qutayba ibn Muslim conquers Transoxiana (modern Uzbekistan and Tajikistan), capturing Bukhara (706), Samarkand (711), and Ferghana (713). Simultaneously, Muhammad ibn Qasim conquers Sind (modern Pakistan) in 711-715. These campaigns bring the most important Silk Road cities and the Indian subcontinent's western gateway into the Islamic world, opening long-term connections with China and India.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Central Asian conquests integrate the Silk Road's most commercially significant cities into the Islamic world; Samarkand and Bukhara become centers of Islamic learning and culture; the Battle of Talas (751) stops further Islamic advance into China but confirms Islamic control of the Silk Road; the Sind conquest begins Islam's long relationship with the Indian subcontinent that eventually produces the Mughal Empire
